itineraries.title: Museum Park Saturday — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: One free campus, all day: an artisan market, a kid-paced gallery tour, drop-in art-making, then a $16 murder mystery across town
itineraries.drive_time: ~15 min from downtown Raleigh to the NCMA on Blue Ridge Rd. NCMA to Raleigh Little Theatre is about 6 min (both sit off Wade Ave).
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$56 (everything on the NCMA campus is free; the optional plant workshop is $40 and Clue is $6–$16)
itineraries.overview: Saturday is mostly sunny and near 89°F, so this one leans on the NCMA — free galleries, a free park, and a first-Saturday artisan market all in one place. Start with an optional 9 AM herbalism workshop in the Museum Park, browse The Market at NCMA from 11, cool off indoors with drop-in art-making, then finish at Raleigh Little Theatre's Clue for under $20.

morning.title: Midtown Farmers' Market
morning.location: The Commons at North Hills, 4150 Main at North Hills St, Raleigh
morning.notes: Optional early stop 10 min from the museum. Go at 8 while it's still under 80°F — this market wraps at noon.

morning.title: Summer Native Medicinal Plants: Passionflower
morning.location: NCMA Museum Park, Welcome Center, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
morning.notes: Ages 16+ and capacity-limited, so register ahead. You leave with a cutting. Skip this leg if you want the day to stay free.

morning.title: Family-Friendly Tours
morning.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
morning.notes: Thirty minutes, built for short attention spans — a good first stop with kids before the market crowd builds.

afternoon.title: The Market at NCMA
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, 2110 Blue Ridge Rd, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: First-Saturday makers market with live music, 11–4. Outdoor: bring a hat and water, and plan to duck into the galleries when it peaks.

afternoon.title: Art on the Dot
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Drop-in art-making, 2:30–4:30, fully indoors and air-conditioned — the natural place to be when the afternoon heat tops out.

evening.title: Clue (High School Edition)
evening.location: Gaddy-Goodwin Teaching Theatre, 301 Pogue Street, Raleigh
evening.notes: Ninety minutes, no intermission. Adults $16, students under 18 $6. Contains gunshots, theatrical violence and flashing lights.

evening.title: Once Upon A One More Time
evening.location: De Ann S. Jones Theatre, 6638 Old Wake Forest Rd, Raleigh
evening.notes: Alternate evening: closing night of Theatre Raleigh ACT's Britney Spears jukebox musical. Pick this or Clue, not both — they start at the same time.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk latte with a fruit-and-nut granola bowl (ask which pastries are made without dairy that morning)
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit
food.notes: Close to Wade Ave on the way to the museum. Menus rotate — confirm the plant-based pastry of the day at the counter.

food.place: Iris (NCMA restaurant) or the market food vendors
food.vegan_dish: unknown — the museum menu rotates seasonally; ask the kitchen what can be made without dairy
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — usually at least one vegetarian entree or salad on the seasonal menu
food.notes: Eating on campus keeps you out of the car. If the market vendors look better, that works too — just confirm ingredients directly with each vendor.

food.vegan_dish: The fully plant-based menu — the fried 'chicken' plate and the tofu banh mi are longtime staples
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything on the menu (the kitchen is entirely meat-free)
food.notes: Downtown Raleigh, entirely vegetarian with most of the menu vegan. Reservations strongly recommended on a Saturday — book before you leave the museum.

alternatives.leg: The Market at NCMA (outdoor, 11:00 AM–4:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk the vendor rows and the Museum Park trails, then picnic on the lawn.
alternatives.rain: The market is outdoors and would thin out fast — move inside to the free NCMA galleries, then catch Art on the Dot at 2:30.

alternatives.good_weather: A comfortable morning walk in the Museum Park before the heat sets in.
alternatives.rain: Ask about the rain policy when you register; if it's called off, the 10:30 family tour and the galleries are both indoors and free.

practical_notes: NCMA parking is free, and so are the galleries and the Museum Park — the only paid item here is the workshop.
Near 89°F and mostly sunny: the outdoor legs are best before 11 AM or after 5 PM. Refill water at the museum.
Register for the Passionflower workshop in advance (ages 16+, limited capacity) — walk-ups are unlikely to get in.
Clue and Once Upon A One More Time both curtain at 7:30 PM in different parts of Raleigh; choose one.
Raleigh Little Theatre's box office reopens at 5:30 PM on show nights; runtime is about 90 minutes.

itineraries.title: Market, Doubleheader & Cocktails — Durham
itineraries.theme: A full Bull City Saturday: the region's best-known market, both halves of a seven-inning doubleheader, and a guided cocktail walk in between
itineraries.drive_time: ~25 min Raleigh → downtown Durham. Everything after the market is walkable: Durham Central Park to the DBAP is about 15 min on foot, and Durham Distillery sits between them.
itineraries.cost_range: $20–$160 (market is free; add a ballgame ticket and, if you want the splurge, the $99 cocktail tour)
itineraries.overview: The Bulls play a scheduled seven-inning doubleheader on Saturday, which turns an ordinary ballpark trip into a day with a gap in the middle. Fill that gap with the Durham Farmers' Market in the morning and, if you're spending, the Bull City Cocktails Tour at 4 PM — it starts and ends within walking distance of the park.

morning.title: Durham Farmers' Market
morning.location: Durham Central Park Pavilion, 501 Foster St, Durham
morning.notes: Under the pavilion, so there's shade even at 89°F. Producer-only: peaches, tomatoes, bread, flowers. Wraps at noon.

afternoon.title: Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers — Doubleheader Game 1
afternoon.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Seven innings, so figure roughly two hours. Buy shade on the first-base side if you can — a 1 PM start in August is the hottest seat of the week.

afternoon.title: Saturday Reflections
afternoon.location: Nasher Museum of Art, 2001 Campus Dr, Durham
afternoon.notes: Quieter, free alternative to the ballpark, 2–3:15 PM — a slow-looking gallery program designed for visitors with memory loss and their companions.

afternoon.title: Bull City Cocktails Tour
afternoon.location: Meets at Durham Distillery, 711 Washington St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Two hours, three cocktails with food pairings at Conniption Lounge, Liberty & Plenty and TaTaco. 21+. Book ahead — it's a small guided group, and it lands you back near the ballpark by 6.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers — Doubleheader Game 2
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: The nightcap, and the better half of the day weather-wise. Also seven innings — you'll be out by roughly 9.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan cake donut plus home fries — the vegan case is a fixture here
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit sandwich
food.notes: Walkable from the market. Gets a long line by 9 on Saturdays — go before the market, not after.

food.place: Market vendors at Durham Central Park
food.vegan_dish: unknown — prepared-food vendors rotate weekly; ask each stall directly
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — produce and bakery stalls are the reliable meat-free option
food.notes: Grab lunch at the market before the 1:05 first pitch, or eat inside the ballpark. Ballpark concessions are cash-light — bring a card.

food.vegan_dish: Plant-based soul-food plate — the tofu-and-collards combination is the house signature
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything on the menu (fully plant-based kitchen)
food.notes: The safest plant-based dinner on this route, but hours are limited and it can close early — call before you drive over, or eat between games.

alternatives.good_weather: Sit in the sun with a lemonade — seven innings goes fast.
alternatives.rain: Storms are only a slight chance Saturday, but a rain delay is always possible. The Nasher (free, 2 PM) and the American Tobacco Campus are both minutes away and indoors.

alternatives.leg: Bull City Cocktails Tour (partly outdoor walking, 4:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: A pleasant downtown walk between three bars.
alternatives.rain: The tour walks between indoor venues, so light rain isn't fatal — bring a compact umbrella and confirm with the operator.

practical_notes: Both games are scheduled seven-inning contests — a doubleheader, not a rain makeup, so expect the pair to run about two hours each.
Park once: the Durham Centre and Corcoran Street decks put you within walking distance of the market, the distillery and the ballpark.
The cocktail tour is 21+ and $99 per person, and it meets at Durham Distillery at 711 Washington St — arrive a few minutes early.
Near 89°F: the 1:05 PM game is the hottest thing on this list. Sunscreen, water, and shade seats if they're available.
If you only want one game, take the 6:45 PM nightcap — cooler, and the atmosphere is better.

itineraries.title: Market Morning, Bourbon & BBQ Evening — Cary
itineraries.theme: A western-Triangle Saturday built around one big ticket: producer-only markets early, then unlimited tastings at Koka Booth
itineraries.drive_time: ~25 min Raleigh → downtown Cary; Cary market to Koka Booth Amphitheatre is about 8 min. Apex is a 10-min detour if you want a second market.
itineraries.cost_range: $45–$110 (markets are free; the festival is $45 general or $79 VIP, plus an optional comedy ticket)
itineraries.overview: The Beer, Bourbon & BBQ Festival takes over Koka Booth on Saturday afternoon — VIP at noon, general admission at 2, everyone out by 6. That leaves the whole morning for Cary's and Apex's Saturday markets, and the evening free for a comedy set once you've handed over the car keys.

morning.title: Cary Downtown Farmers Market
morning.notes: Producer-only and compact — an easy hour. Closes at noon.

morning.title: Apex Farmers Market
morning.location: The Depot, 220 N Salem St, Apex
morning.notes: Optional second market beside the historic Apex depot, 10 min south. Downtown Apex is a pleasant walk afterward.

afternoon.title: Beer, Bourbon & BBQ Festival — Saturday Session
afternoon.location: Koka Booth Amphitheatre, 8003 Regency Parkway, Cary
afternoon.notes: VIP gets in at noon, general admission at 2, and it ends at 6. Admission includes a sampling glass for all-you-care-to-taste beer and bourbon; BBQ is sold separately. Clear-bag policy applies.

evening.title: Dale Jones
evening.location: Raleigh Improv, Cary
evening.notes: Ten minutes from Koka Booth and it starts right after the festival ends. ID must match the ticket name, and third-party tickets are refused.

evening.title: Andrew Orolfo
evening.location: Raleigh Improv, Cary
evening.notes: Later set at the same club if 6:30 is too soon after a tasting festival.

food.place: Once in a Blue Moon Bakery & Cafe
food.vegan_dish: unknown — ask which pastries are made without butter or eggs that morning
food.vegetarian_dish: Pastries and quiche are the standbys
food.notes: Walking distance from the Cary market. Eat before the festival — you'll want food in you before a tasting session.

food.vegan_dish: Black-bean-and-plantain arepa or bowl, no cheese or crema, with the avocado sauce
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese arepa with black beans and sweet plantains
food.notes: Fast, cheap and genuinely good for plant-based eaters — a solid base layer before 2 PM. Confirm sauces at the counter.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — a whole-hog BBQ festival rarely runs a vegan plate; eat at Guasaca first if you're plant-based
food.vegetarian_dish: Sides (slaw, beans, mac) where vendors offer them
food.notes: Food is sold separately from admission. Plant-based attendees should treat lunch as the real meal and the festival as drinks.

alternatives.good_weather: Koka Booth's lawn under mostly sunny skies — bring a hat.
alternatives.rain: It's a rain-or-shine amphitheater event; check the festival's policy before travelling and bring a poncho rather than a large umbrella (clear-bag rules apply).

alternatives.good_weather: Do both Cary and Apex — they're 10 minutes apart.
alternatives.rain: Markets run in light rain but vendors thin out; go straight to Cary's and skip the Apex leg.

practical_notes: Do not drive after the festival. Designated-driver tickets are $25 on site, and a rideshare from Koka Booth to downtown Cary is short.
General admission opens at 2 PM, VIP at noon; the session ends at 6 PM for everyone. Two-day passes are $165 if you also want Friday.
Koka Booth enforces a clear-bag policy — check it before you pack.
Buy festival tickets online in advance; the organizers warn that day-of tickets may not be available.
Near 89°F and mostly sunny: alternate tastings with water, and use the shaded areas near the lake.

itineraries.title: Market to Cat's Cradle — Carrboro & Chapel Hill
itineraries.theme: The classic Orange County Saturday: a 7 AM producer market, an afternoon of bookshops and co-op lunch, and a club show at night
itineraries.drive_time: ~35 min Raleigh → Carrboro. Once you're there almost nothing needs the car: the Town Commons, Weaver Street Market and Cat's Cradle are all within a few blocks.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 (both markets are free; budget for a show ticket and lunch)
itineraries.overview: Carrboro's market opens at 7 AM — the earliest in the Triangle and the best way to beat an 89°F Saturday. Spend the morning between the Town Commons and Weaver Street, browse Chapel Hill's Franklin Street in the afternoon heat, then pick from three club shows within walking distance that night.

morning.title: Carrboro Farmers' Market
morning.location: Carrboro Town Commons, 301 W Main St, Carrboro
morning.notes: Opens at 7 and runs to noon — one of the state's best producer-only markets. Arrive early both for the heat and for the good tomatoes.

morning.title: Chapel Hill Farmers' Market
morning.location: University Place, 201 S Estes Dr, Chapel Hill
morning.notes: Optional second market 8 minutes east, also finishing at noon.

afternoon.title: Franklin Street browsing and a co-op lunch
afternoon.notes: No ticketed event fits this slot, which is fine — the bookstores and record shops are air-conditioned, and that matters at 89°F.

evening.title: The Dear Hunter — The Road to Sunya Tour 2026
evening.location: Cat's Cradle, 300 E Main St, Carrboro
evening.notes: Main-room show with Motherfolk and K Sera. Doors 6:30, show 7:30 — walkable from the market site.

evening.title: Islander — The Dead Youth Tour
evening.location: Local 506, 506 W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: Heavier option, a mile east on Franklin Street. Doors 7, show 7:30.

evening.title: The Rattletraps Album Release Party
evening.location: Cat's Cradle Back Room, 300 E Main St, Carrboro
evening.notes: Same building as the Cradle main room, smaller space, local bill with Max Lane and Beeper — the lower-key pick.

food.vegan_dish: Hot-bar tofu scramble and roasted vegetables (the hot bar is labelled for vegan items)
food.vegetarian_dish: Pastries, yoghurt and the hot bar
food.notes: Directly beside the market on the Town Commons, and the labelling makes it the easiest plant-based call of the day. Lawn seating outside.

food.vegan_dish: Chana masala or the daily vegan curry with rice — the kitchen marks vegan dishes clearly
food.vegetarian_dish: Most of the menu; the thali is the easy pick
food.notes: Long-standing Franklin Street kitchen that takes plant-based cooking seriously. Confirm the day's vegan curry when you order.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — ask whether the veggie patty and bun are dairy-free that day
food.vegetarian_dish: Veggie burger with the usual toppings
food.notes: Quick pre-show dinner near Local 506. If you want a guaranteed vegan dinner instead, eat at Weaver Street before the show.

alternatives.good_weather: The whole point of the day — walk it slowly and eat breakfast on the Weaver Street lawn.
alternatives.rain: The market runs in light rain with fewer vendors; if it's heavy, Weaver Street Market next door is indoors and open.
Bookstores, record shops and the Ackland Art Museum are all indoors within a few blocks.

practical_notes: Carrboro's market is producer-only and opens at 7 AM — the earliest start of any Triangle market this week.
Park once in downtown Carrboro: the market, Weaver Street and Cat's Cradle are all walkable from the same lot.
Three shows overlap on Saturday night — the Cradle main room (7:30), Local 506 (7:30) and the Back Room (8:00). Pick one before you buy.
Cat's Cradle ticket links go through Etix; prices weren't posted on the venue calendar, so check at checkout.
Near 89°F: front-load the outdoor legs into the morning and treat the afternoon as indoor time.

itineraries.title: Rain-Proof Family Sunday — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: Thunderstorms are likely, so this Sunday is built indoors: a free Hot Wheels takeover, an audio-described matinee, and a car show you can catch before the sky turns
itineraries.drive_time: ~20 min from downtown Raleigh to Triangle Town Center; Triangle Town Center to Raleigh Little Theatre is about 20 min.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$32 (Hot Wheels and the car show are free with free parking; Clue is $6–$16 a seat)
itineraries.overview: Sunday brings showers and thunderstorms likely with a high near 87°F, so almost everything here is under a roof. The free Hot Wheels event fills the old Macy's at Triangle Town Center from 10 to 5 — with a race-track contest 11 to 4 — and the outdoor car show is early enough to beat the afternoon storms. Then it's an audio-described matinee of Clue, or free art-making at the NCMA.

morning.title: Caffeine and Machines Car Show
morning.location: Triangle Town Center parking lot, 5959 Triangle Town Blvd, Raleigh
morning.notes: Outdoors, 10 AM–2 PM. Do this first — the storm risk climbs through the afternoon. Free parking on site.

morning.title: Raleigh World of Hot Wheels
morning.location: Triangle Town Center, former Macy's space, 5959 Triangle Town Blvd, Raleigh
morning.notes: Indoors, 10–5, with a race-track contest 11–4. Entry and parking are both free — the single best rain hedge of the week for kids.

afternoon.title: Public Tour
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Docent-led hour through the collection. Free, indoor, and 20 min from the mall if you'd rather swap the mall for a museum.

afternoon.title: Art on the Dot
afternoon.location: North Carolina Museum of Art, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Drop-in art-making, 2:30–4:30, indoors and free — a good landing spot when the rain arrives.

afternoon.title: Clue (High School Edition) — Audio Described Matinee
afternoon.location: Gaddy-Goodwin Teaching Theatre, 301 Pogue Street, Raleigh
afternoon.notes: Sunday 3 PM matinee with audio description available. Ninety minutes; adults $16, students under 18 $6. Contains gunshots and flashing lights.

evening.title: The Bleeding Hearts Sunday Funday Album Release
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall, 224 S Blount St, Raleigh
evening.notes: An early, indoor show — doors 3, music 4 — so you're home before a late storm. Not a kids' room, though.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: If the radar clears, the Sunday series finale is a 25-min drive. Outdoor, so check the forecast before committing.

food.vegan_dish: Oat-milk latte and a fruit-and-granola bowl
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit
food.notes: Quick stop before the 10 AM car show. Confirm dairy-free pastries at the counter — the case changes daily.

food.vegan_dish: Falafel plate with hummus, tabbouleh and pita (skip the yoghurt sauce)
food.vegetarian_dish: Spinach pies and the mezze plate
food.notes: Reliable, fast and unusually good for plant-based eaters — the mezze side of the menu is almost entirely vegan. Indoor seating.

food.vegan_dish: The plant-based menu in full — the fried 'chicken' plate is the house standard
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything (fully meat-free kitchen)
food.notes: Downtown, entirely vegetarian, mostly vegan. Sunday hours are shorter than weekends — check before you go and reserve if you can.

alternatives.leg: Caffeine and Machines Car Show (outdoor, 10:00 AM–2:00 PM)
alternatives.good_weather: Walk the lot in the morning, then head inside for Hot Wheels.
alternatives.rain: Skip it entirely — the Hot Wheels event is 100 feet away, indoors, free, and runs until 5.

alternatives.good_weather: Drive over for the series finale.
alternatives.rain: Trade it for the 3 PM Clue matinee or the 4 PM Pour House show — both indoors, both in Raleigh.

practical_notes: Showers and thunderstorms are likely Sunday with a high near 87°F — this itinerary is deliberately weighted indoors.
Hot Wheels entry and parking are both free, and it runs 10–5 with the race-track contest 11–4. It is the reliable all-day fallback.
The 3 PM Clue performance is the run's audio-described show; mention access needs when booking.
The NCMA galleries, park and both Sunday programs are free — no ticket needed to walk in.
The Pour House show is 4 PM, not evening — don't plan dinner first.

itineraries.title: Food Truck Friday & Beer Garden Concert — Durham
itineraries.theme: A nearly-free Friday night in RTP and downtown Durham: Jamaican food off a truck, live music in a beer garden, then drag bingo
itineraries.drive_time: ~25 min Raleigh → Glass Jug RTP. RTP to downtown Durham is about 15 min; the ballpark and Carolina Theatre are a block apart downtown.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$45 (no cover for the food truck or the beer-garden concert — you pay for what you eat and drink)
itineraries.overview: Friday hits 90°F and stays sunny, which is exactly right for a beer garden once the sun drops. Campbell's Jamaican Cafe parks at the Glass Jug in RTP at 5, The Hourglass Kids play the garden 6 to 9, and neither has a cover. If you'd rather be downtown, drag bingo at the Glass Jug's Durham taproom starts at 7, the Bulls are home at 6:45, and The Mavericks play Fletcher Hall at 8.

afternoon.title: Bull City Cocktails Tour
afternoon.location: Meets at Durham Distillery, 711 Washington St, Durham
afternoon.notes: Optional splurge that bookends the evening — two hours, three cocktails with food pairings, 21+. Ends at 6, leaving the night open downtown.

evening.title: Food Truck Friday — Campbell's Jamaican Cafe
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham
evening.notes: No cover; you only pay the truck. 5–8 PM. Free parking at the door.

evening.title: Beer Garden Concert Series with The Hourglass Kids
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), Durham
evening.notes: Outdoor beer-garden set, 6–9, overlapping the food truck. At 90°F, arrive nearer 7 when the shade reaches the garden.

evening.title: Durham Bulls vs Gwinnett Stripers
evening.location: Durham Bulls Athletic Park, 409 Blackwell St, Durham
evening.notes: Alternative Friday night downtown. Outdoor, and 90°F at first pitch — buy shade if you can.

evening.title: Drag Bingo at Glass Jug Downtown
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab — Downtown Durham
evening.notes: Indoor and air-conditioned, 7–9 PM, 15 min from RTP. The obvious move if the heat wins.

evening.title: The Mavericks & Friends
evening.location: Carolina Theatre of Durham, Fletcher Hall, 309 W Morgan St, Durham
evening.notes: The indoor headline option downtown — genre-blending country-rock in Fletcher Hall, a block from the ballpark.

food.vegan_dish: Vegetable bibimbap without egg, with tofu
food.vegetarian_dish: Bibimbap or the vegetable dumplings
food.notes: If you're making a full day of it in Durham. Confirm that the gochujang and broth are meat-free when you order.

food.place: Campbell's Jamaican Cafe truck at Glass Jug RTP
food.vegan_dish: unknown — many Jamaican menus run an ital or callaloo option, but check the board on arrival
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — rice and peas plus plantains are the usual meat-free combination; confirm at the window
food.notes: This is dinner if you stay for the concert. Plant-based eaters should have a backup — see Vegan Flava Cafe.

food.vegan_dish: Plant-based soul-food plate with collards and mac
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything on the menu (fully plant-based)
food.notes: The dependable plant-based dinner in Durham, but hours are limited — call ahead rather than assuming it's open at 8.

alternatives.good_weather: Sunny and 90°F — stay in the garden as the sun drops and the shade comes across.
alternatives.rain: No rain expected Friday, but the RTP taproom is indoors and open; drag bingo downtown at 7 is the other indoor option.

alternatives.good_weather: A fine night for a ballgame once the sun is off the seats.
alternatives.rain: The Carolina Theatre (8 PM) and drag bingo (7 PM) are both indoors and minutes away.

practical_notes: Both Glass Jug RTP events are free to attend — budget only for food and beer.
Glass Jug RTP is at 5410 NC-55 Suite V with free surface parking right outside; downtown Durham needs a deck (Durham Centre or Corcoran Street).
90°F and sunny: the beer garden is much more pleasant after 7 PM than at 5.
The cocktail tour is 21+, $99, and books out — reserve before the day if you want it.
Four options overlap between 6:45 and 8 PM downtown; pick one and don't try to stack them.

itineraries.title: Poetry in the Park, Then Pick a Show — Raleigh
itineraries.theme: A free Friday evening on the Dix Park porches, then four downtown Raleigh venues within a few blocks of each other
itineraries.drive_time: Dix Park is ~5 min from downtown Raleigh; the Pour House, Lincoln Theatre and Kings are all walkable from one another. Goodnights and ComedyWorx are 10 min west.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$50 (Poetry in the Park costs nothing; shows run from $15 to about $46)
itineraries.overview: Start free: Poetry in the Park runs 6 to 8 on the porches at Dix Park, five minutes from downtown, with the skyline in view. After that, downtown Raleigh has four rooms going — tribute rock at the Lincoln, more tributes at the Pour House, stand-up at Goodnights, and improv at ComedyWorx — and you can walk between the first two.

evening.title: Poetry in the Park
evening.location: House of Many Porches Market, Dix Park, 701 Palmer Dr., Raleigh
evening.notes: Outdoors on the porches, 6–8 PM. It's 90°F and sunny, so bring water and take the shaded side. Free parking in the park.

evening.title: Derrick Stroup
evening.location: Goodnights Comedy Club, 401 Woodburn Rd., Raleigh
evening.notes: Two shows Friday, 7:00 and 9:15 — take the late one if you want the full two hours of poetry first.

evening.title: The Big Sham: The Whom w/ Tributes to The Beatles, Alabama Shakes & The Kinks
evening.location: The Pour House Music Hall, 224 S Blount St, Raleigh
evening.notes: The cheapest ticket downtown and a short walk from the Lincoln. Doors 7, show 8.

evening.title: The ComedyWorx Show
evening.location: ComedyWorx, 3801 Hillsborough St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Competitive improv where the audience calls the shots, 8–9:30. Late option: BEST OF Mad Lab at 10.

evening.title: Shortest Straw (Metallica Tribute) & Undertow (Tool Tribute)
evening.location: Lincoln Theatre, 126 E Cabarrus St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Doors 7:30, show 8:30; $22.25 day-of. The latest start of the four, so it pairs best with the full poetry session.

evening.title: BEST OF Mad Lab
evening.location: ComedyWorx, 3801 Hillsborough St, Raleigh
evening.notes: Late-night experimental improv, 10–11:30, if the night still has life in it.

food.vegan_dish: Mushroom or bean tacos on corn tortillas, no crema or cheese
food.vegetarian_dish: Cheese-and-bean quesadilla or veggie tacos
food.notes: Casual and quick if you're downtown early. Confirm the beans are made without lard.

food.vegan_dish: Vegetable-and-tofu larb or the vegetarian curry ordered without fish sauce — say so explicitly
food.vegetarian_dish: Crispy rice salad and the vegetable curry
food.notes: Laotian restaurant on Blount Street, a block from the Pour House. Book ahead on a Friday; fish sauce is common, so state dietary needs clearly.

food.vegan_dish: Fully plant-based menu — the fried 'chicken' plate and tofu banh mi
food.vegetarian_dish: Everything (meat-free kitchen)
food.notes: The safest plant-based dinner downtown and a short walk to the venues. Reserve — Friday fills up.

alternatives.good_weather: Sunny and 90°F — take a blanket and the shaded porch side, and stay for the whole two hours.
alternatives.rain: No rain forecast Friday, but if it turns, all four evening venues are indoors and start between 7 and 8:30.

alternatives.good_weather: The Pour House, Lincoln Theatre and Kings are a few blocks apart — leave the car in one deck.
alternatives.rain: Same walk, shorter: pick a single venue and park beside it.

practical_notes: Poetry in the Park is free and parking at Dix Park is free — the whole first half of this evening costs nothing.
Downtown Raleigh street parking is free after 5 PM on weekdays; the Moore Square and Blount Street decks cover the Pour House and Lincoln.
Show times ladder nicely: poetry 6–8, Pour House at 8, Lincoln at 8:30, Goodnights late show at 9:15. Two are realistic in one night.
The Lincoln Theatre price range is wide ($16.25–$178.25) because of VIP tiers — the low end is a normal ticket.
90°F and sunny: hydrate during the outdoor leg before you sit in a warm club.

itineraries.title: Gardens, Storytime & a Run Club — Durham Thursday
itineraries.theme: A gentle Bull City Thursday: bilingual storytime in an art museum, a native-plant garden walk, $5 mystery beer, and a free group run
itineraries.drive_time: ~25 min Raleigh → Duke campus. The Nasher and Duke Gardens are 5 min apart; Ponysaurus and the Glass Jug are both about 10 min east in downtown Durham.
itineraries.cost_range: $0–$25 (storytime is free, the garden walk is $10, mystery beer is $5, the run clubs are free)
itineraries.overview: Thursday is the quiet end of the week and it stacks well around Duke. Durham County Library reads in Spanish and English inside the Nasher galleries at 10:30, the Blomquist native-plant tour goes out at 11 for $10, and by evening there are two free group runs and a $5 mystery pour. Note that this date sits past the National Weather Service's seven-day window, so there is no forecast attached yet — check before the outdoor legs.

morning.title: Bilingual Story Time / Tiempo de Historias Bilingues
morning.location: Nasher Museum of Art, 2001 Campus Dr, Durham
morning.notes: Free, indoors, 10:30–11:30, with art-looking afterward. The family pick — but it overlaps the garden walk, so choose one.

morning.title: Walk on the Wild Side
morning.location: Sarah P. Duke Gardens, 420 Anderson St, Durham
morning.notes: Staff-led hour through the Blomquist Garden of Native Plants, $10. Outdoors — bring water and register ahead.

afternoon.title: Mystery Beer Thursdays
afternoon.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab (RTP), 5410 NC-55 Suite V, Durham
afternoon.notes: Bartender's choice for $5, all day until 10 PM. A cheap, unhurried afternoon stop between the gardens and the evening runs.

evening.title: Pony Run Thursdays with Fleet Feet
evening.location: Ponysaurus Brewing Co., 219 Hood St, Durham
evening.notes: Free 3- or 5-mile routes led by Fleet Feet, then beer on the patio. 6:15–8 PM. No signup needed.

evening.title: Latinos & Latinas Run Club at Glass Jug Downtown
evening.location: The Glass Jug Beer Lab — Downtown Durham
evening.notes: The other free Thursday run, from the downtown taproom, 6:30–8:30. Pick whichever start point suits you.

evening.title: Big Tow with Nathan Arizona & The New Mexicans
evening.location: Local 506, 506 W Franklin St, Chapel Hill
evening.notes: If you want music to finish on, Local 506 is 20 min west of Duke. Doors 7, show 8.

food.vegan_dish: Vegan cake donut and home fries
food.vegetarian_dish: Egg-and-cheese biscuit sandwich
food.notes: Ten minutes from the Nasher and open early — the easy start before a 10:30 storytime.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — the menu is small and seasonal; ask what can be made without dairy
food.vegetarian_dish: unknown — usually a salad or sandwich option
food.notes: Convenient if you're already at the museum. Hours are tied to the museum's, so confirm before planning lunch around it.

food.vegan_dish: unknown — ask whether a pie can be built without cheese; the vegetable toppings are the plant-based route
food.vegetarian_dish: Margherita or the seasonal vegetable pie
food.notes: Downtown Durham, walkable from Ponysaurus after the run. No reservations, so expect a wait on the patio.

alternatives.leg: Walk on the Wild Side (outdoor, 11:00 AM)
alternatives.good_weather: An hour in the Blomquist native-plant garden — shaded for much of the route.
alternatives.rain: Swap to the Nasher's bilingual storytime at 10:30 (free, indoors) and spend the rest of the morning in the galleries.

alternatives.good_weather: Either route, then beer at the taproom.
alternatives.rain: Both start at breweries — skip the run and stay inside for the beer, or head to Local 506 for the 8 PM show.

practical_notes: August 6 falls outside the National Weather Service's current seven-day forecast, so no weather is attached to this day yet — re-check the forecast before the garden walk and the runs.
The 10:30 storytime and the 11:00 garden walk overlap; they're 5 minutes apart but you can only do one.
Register in advance for Walk on the Wild Side ($10) — it's a staff-led tour with limited space.
Both run clubs are free and need no signup; they finish at a bar, so plan your ride accordingly.
Duke Gardens parking is paid by the hour at the Anderson Street entrance; the Nasher has its own free lot.
